headline: EQUINOX GOLD + ORLA MINING COMBINATION COMPLETE — North America's New Senior Gold Producer Born With 1.1M oz Annual Output
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX: EQX) and Orla Mining Ltd. completed their business combination on July 31, 2026, creating what the companies describe as North America's new senior gold producer. The combined entity will produce approximately 1.1 million ounces of gold annually, with a stated path to more than 1.9 million ounces as high-quality North American growth projects advance. Orla shareholders received 1.00 Equinox Gold common share and US$0.0001 in cash per Orla share; Orla will be delisted from the TSX and NYSE American. The transaction consolidates a portfolio of producing and development-stage assets across the Americas — creating a scaled North American gold platform at a moment when institutional capital is actively seeking size and liquidity in the gold equity space. The new company begins trading on a combined basis immediately.

headline: ANGLOGOLD Q2: PROFIT +58% TO $1.01B, FCF +36% TO $727M — $2B Buyback Approved, $364M Dividend Declared; EBITDA Surges 46% to $2.0B
snippet: AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU) reported Q2 2026 results on July 31 showing headline earnings of $1.01 billion — a 58% year-on-year increase — as higher gold prices offset lower production volumes. Free cash flow rose 36% year-on-year to $727 million in the quarter and $1.9 billion for the first half of 2026. The company declared an interim Q2 dividend of $364 million ($0.72 per share), bringing H1 2026 dividends to $949 million versus $469 million in H1 2025 — a 102% year-on-year increase in distributions. EBITDA for Q2 reached $2.0 billion, up 46% year-on-year. Shareholders approved a $2 billion share buyback program at the July 23 AGM. For investors tracking the capital return acceleration thesis across senior gold producers, AngloGold's combination of record profit, a fresh $2 billion buyback, and doubling dividends in one year makes it one of the clearest beneficiaries of the $4,000+ gold environment.

headline: ANGLO AMERICAN COPPER: $2.9B EBITDA AT 60% MARGIN IN H1 — Overall EBITDA +35% to $4B; Anglo-Teck Supermajor Merger on Track for September 2026 Close
snippet: Anglo American reported H1 2026 results on July 30 with underlying EBITDA of $4.0 billion for continuing operations — up 35% year-on-year — as its copper segment generated EBITDA of $2.9 billion at a 60% margin, reflecting record copper prices averaging above $6 per pound for the half. CEO Duncan Wanblad noted that capital intensity in mining has risen materially ahead of inflation and that development timelines continue to extend, structural factors that support the case for sustained elevated copper prices. The transformative Anglo-Teck merger, which will create a copper-focused global metals champion, remains on track with an expected completion window of September 2026 to March 2027. First-half copper production was 343,600 tonnes against full-year guidance of 700,000–760,000 tonnes, with the company on pace to meet its annual target.

headline: CAPSTONE COPPER 7th STRAIGHT RECORD EBITDA: $354M +64% YOY — 51,759 Tonnes at $6.22/lb Realized; Debt Continues Falling Despite EPS Miss (TSX: CS)
snippet: Capstone Copper Corp. (TSX: CS) reported its seventh consecutive record adjusted EBITDA on July 30 — $354 million for Q2 2026, up 64% year-on-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter — as the mid-tier Americas copper producer benefited from a realized copper price of $6.22 per pound on 51,759 tonnes of consolidated copper production at C1 cash costs of $2.82 per pound. The LME copper average of $6.05 per pound in Q2 2026 was 40% higher year-on-year. Despite a modest EPS miss relative to consensus, shares rose 3.52% as investors focused on the continued debt reduction trajectory and an advancing growth pipeline. For TSX-V and ASX copper explorers, Capstone's seven consecutive record EBITDA quarters at these C1 costs illustrates the sustained economics available to projects that can reach production in the current copper price environment.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC SILVER Q2: REVENUE +57% TO $415M, FCF $194M, EBITDA +110% — Three Mines Raise Guidance; Operating Leverage Thesis Confirmed at $59 Silver (TSX/NYSE: AG)
source_name: Investing News Network / First Majestic Silver
snippet: First Majestic Silver Corp. (TSX/NYSE: AG) reported Q2 2026 financial results on July 30 with revenue up 57% year-on-year to $415.5 million — 60% derived from silver — while EBITDA surged 110% to $252.3 million and net earnings more than doubled to $109.4 million ($0.22 per share). Free cash flow of $194.6 million more than doubled from $77.9 million in the prior year. The company raised silver production guidance at three of four operating mines: Los Gatos +5%, San Dimas +13%, La Encantada +19%, and raised gold guidance at Santa Elena +10%, reflecting sustained metallurgical outperformance. For investors tracking the operating leverage thesis for primary silver producers at $59 silver, the 57% revenue gain against a 57% realized silver price improvement confirms the business model is executing precisely as expected — and the raised guidance signals production momentum that will compound into Q3.

headline: PUREPOINT URANIUM HITS 53,300 CPS OVER 5.6 METRES AT NOVA DISCOVERY — Saskatchewan High-Grade Athabasca Intercept Consistent With Previous 8.1% U3O8; Assays Pending (TSXV: PTU)
snippet: Purepoint Uranium Group Inc. (TSXV: PTU) reported on July 30 that hole NV26-11 — the final hole of the first phase of the 2026 summer drill program at the Nova Discovery on the Dorado Project in Saskatchewan — intersected 5.6 metres of continuous radioactivity from 337.9 to 343.5 metres depth, averaging 11,730 counts per second from the downhole probe with a peak reading of 53,300 cps. Laboratory assays remain pending. The Dorado Project is a 50/50 joint venture between Purepoint and IsoEnergy Ltd. (TSX: ISO); previous drilling at Nova returned peak grades of 8.1% U3O8 over 0.4 metres. In the Athabasca Basin context, a 53,300 cps peak from a downhole probe at the unconformity is a highly encouraging radiometric indicator — consistent with the CPS-to-grade relationships observed at historical high-grade uranium discoveries in the same structural corridor. The second phase of the 2026 program is expected to continue through August.

headline: TRUMP INVOKES DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT ON CRITICAL MINERAL SCRAP — New Export Curbs Cover Old Batteries and E-Waste; Commerce Gets Authority to Block Shipments to Adversaries
snippet: President Trump invoked the Defense Production Act on July 30 to restrict U.S. exports of recoverable critical minerals — targeting old batteries, electronics, and other e-waste streams that contain rare earths, lithium, cobalt, and other strategic materials. The Commerce Secretary received authority to implement export restrictions, preventing scrap containing critical minerals from being shipped to adversarial processors abroad. The action builds on a July 20 executive order that restricted defense contractor waivers for critical mineral sourcing from China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. The policy framework signals that Washington now treats even end-of-life critical mineral streams — not just primary mine output — as a national security resource, adding another layer to the de-coupling effort that is directly relevant to Western mining project economics: reducing Chinese processor access to recycled feedstocks increases demand pressure on primary supply.

headline: CHINA IMPORTS 173 TONNES OF GOLD IN JUNE — 2-Year Monthly High; H1 2026 Total Reaches 820t, Second-Highest First Half Ever, as Retail Buyers Bought $4,000 Dip
snippet: China imported 173 tonnes of gold in June 2026 — the highest monthly total in more than two years and the third consecutive month of increasing imports — as Chinese retail investors aggressively bought the dip when gold fell from $4,500+ in early June to approximately $4,000. H1 2026 Chinese gold imports total approximately 820 tonnes, the second-highest first-half total on record, just 10 tonnes below the record set in 2025. The data reinforces the structural physical demand floor under the gold market: when Western institutional sentiment turns cautious on gold during a corrective phase, Chinese retail buyers absorb physical supply at scale, establishing a demand backstop that has prevented the kind of deep corrections seen in prior gold cycles. For investors tracking the macro setup for the autumn rally, a Chinese retail buyer who stepped in at $4,000 is sitting on gains as gold approaches $4,100 — creating incentive for further buying on confirmation of the trend.

headline: ZIMBABWE LITHIUM EXPORTS +230% TO $782M IN H1 2026 — Local Processing Mandate Bearing Fruit as Raw Concentrate Ban Approaches January 2027
snippet: Zimbabwe's Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube confirmed that the country exported $782 million worth of lithium products in H1 2026 — a 230% year-on-year surge from $237 million in H1 2025 — as the government's local beneficiation mandate forces Chinese mining operators to process material within Zimbabwe before export. Spodumene concentrates accounted for $672.8 million of the total; lithium sulphate from the country's first processing plant (commissioned April 2026) contributed $73.2 million. Zimbabwe plans to ban raw lithium concentrate exports from January 2027 entirely, which will further shift the export mix toward higher-value downstream products. For global lithium supply watchers, Zimbabwe's surge represents new production capacity entering the market almost exclusively on Chinese supply chains — under a preferential access framework that Western battery manufacturers and car companies cannot access at the same terms, adding a structural supply asymmetry to the battery metals equation.

headline: GOLD MINERS' Q2: 12th STRAIGHT QUARTER OF HUGE EARNINGS — Stocks at Most-Oversold in 2.8 Years Despite Near-Record Fundamentals; Adam Hamilton Says Autumn Rally Sets Up Re-Rating
snippet: In his weekly Zeal LLC analysis at GoldSeek, Adam Hamilton argues that Q2 2026 will prove gold miners' second-best quarter ever — their 12th consecutive quarter of substantial earnings growth — and that the Q2 results now beginning to land are landing into technically extreme conditions: GDX experienced a 36.5% drawdown over 4.3 months, pushing gold stocks to their most-oversold levels in 2.8 years relative to their 200-day moving average. The core analytical observation is a stark disconnect: gold-stock prices are priced for a $2,500 gold world while the companies are generating cash flows consistent with $4,000+ gold. Hamilton's argument is that when the hard Q2 earnings data hits consensus desks this week — near-record profits at near-record margins — the re-rating catalyst will coincide with the seasonal launchpad for gold's autumn rally. For junior mining investors, the analysis provides a framework for understanding why the sector has underperformed spot gold since January's all-time high, and why the H2 2026 setup looks structurally different.
